title: Beginning performance and mere preparation
summary: Beginning the performance invited by an offer can have a different legal effect from merely preparing to perform. The wording of the offer and the actual conduct determine the distinction.
notes:
White’s purchase and work on ordinary materials did not sufficiently communicate acceptance of the proposed office job. The assigned Ever-Tite passages treat loading trucks and transporting materials as commencement under a clause expressly allowing that means of acceptance. Under Restatement § 45, beginning invited performance can create an option protecting completion when the offer permits acceptance only by performance. Drennan separately concerns reliance before acceptance of an offer seeking a return promise. These routes should not be combined into a rule that all expenditures accept an offer.

White’s generic private carpentry preparation did not manifest acceptance. Ever-Tite’s loading and dispatch of materials began the performance its form invited. Section 45 protects beginning or tendering the performance of a performance-only offer; § 87(2), discussed through Drennan, asks separately about preparatory reliance. A single label such as “started work” obscures the different legal functions.
